first.rationale: Prior evidence indicates signup and onboarding simplification durably improve activation, completion, and time-to-value. This directly addresses the current onboarding decline and likely contributes to recovering activation, while avoiding promotional pricing's documented 30-day retention harm. Verify the two onboarding records before committing; evaluate qualified activation and retention alongside completion.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying the self-serve onboarding flow, prioritizing removal of nonessential steps and fields. Verified evidence shows shortened onboarding increased completion 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and improved 30-day retention 3%; SMB signup simplification increased qualified revenue 4%. This directly addresses both current declines without adopting promotional pricing, whose retention harm makes it unsuitable for sustainable revenue. Measure qualified revenue and 30-day retention by segment; the SMB record's 1% retention decline means retention must be a guardrail.

final2.rationale: Keep the onboarding-simplification experiment. It directly addresses the 4% completion and 6% activation declines and has verified evidence of improved completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention. The competitor's price cut makes promotional pricing tempting for price-sensitive SMBs, but inherited evidence shows it materially harms 30-day retention, conflicting with the objective of sustainable qualified revenue. Segment results and enforce qualified-revenue and retention guardrails, especially for SMBs where signup simplification had a small retention decline.
